transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?
I came in because I feel wound up almost all the time. It’s like my body is bracing for the next bad thing, even when I’m just sitting at my desk or trying to enjoy dance night.
Did something very frightening or traumatic happen to you before these feelings started?
No, I can’t think of anything like that. There wasn’t one specific frightening event before this started, at least not that I can point to.
Are these feelings mainly triggered when you’re around other people or might be watched or judged by them?
I don’t think it’s mainly about being watched or judged. I mean, that can be uncomfortable sometimes, but these feelings come up even when I’m alone or just doing normal things.
Do you ever get sudden surges of intense fear or discomfort that peak within minutes?
I’m not sure. I don’t think I get those sudden, really intense spikes that peak fast like that. It feels more like I’m tense or uneasy for a long time rather than a big rush all at once.
When you start feeling worried or on edge, is it hard for you to control or stop the worrying?

Yes, it is. Even if I tell myself I already checked the spreadsheet or sent the email, my mind keeps going back to it. Then one “what if” turns into a bunch more, and it can take a while before I can pull myself out of it.
Do you find yourself worrying about a lot of different parts of your life, rather than mainly one specific thing?

Yes, definitely. It doesn’t stay on one thing. I’ll start out worrying about the condo, and then it jumps to whether my cousin is upset with me, or if I’m going to mess up on a support call at work, or whether I’ll ever save enough money or move forward in my life. It kind of bounces around.
Have you been feeling this worried and on edge for at least six months?
Yes. It’s been about nine months now, since the condo loan started moving toward foreclosure. That’s when it really started feeling constant.
